content:
- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the early part of the 30-day window, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 35.63, 36.62), model forecasts overshoot and then correct, indicating poor handling of volatility or lagged response.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks or troughs.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; lack of volatility clustering or sudden jumps in true values is not reflected.
- Model underreacts to recent high true values, especially in the last 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts often start too low and then rise too slowly — suggesting a bias toward conservative or “safe” estimates.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20), possibly due to ignoring recent upward momentum.
- Forecasts are not sensitive to the true value of the most recent day in history — often ignoring the last 1–2 data points.
